title: The Kiln and the Hand
logline: A potter's family works a week's batch from wet clay to a fired pot, reading hardness, wetness, warmth and air in their hands long before any of it has a name.
human_question: When a potter's hands turn earth, water, fire and air into a pot, whose making is it: the potter's, or the elements'?

premise.story: One household's working week: clay dug and soaked, thrown or shaped, dried in the wind, fired, and opened, told through the potter's own decisions, orders and losses.
premise.place: A traditional pottery-making household or small workshop where the wheel, the drying racks and the kiln set the week's rhythm.
premise.experience: The pull and give of wet clay, the smell of wet earth, the heat of the kiln, and the moment a fired pot is tapped to hear whether it rings true or has cracked.

concept_links.why: The potter's hands work exactly the four great elements the source names: resistance (earth), cohesion (water), heat (fire) and the air that dries and lightens. The proportion of each, judged by hand, is what makes clay behave differently from stone or oil.
A lump of clay changes colour, hardness and smell together as it dries and fires: the source's own point that matter is a changing pattern kept up by its conditions, not a fixed thing.
Wet clay is one thoroughly mixed thing with no separable ingredients, close to the source's own flour-ball image for how matter never arises alone.

what_camera_could_observe: Clay dug, soaked and kneaded until it binds
The potter's hands and feet at the wheel, judging firmness by touch alone
Pots drying in shade and wind, then loaded into the kiln
The kiln opened: pots tapped and listened to, a cracked piece set aside
A finished pot leaving with a buyer, or staying unsold
what_must_be_real: The potter's own orders, prices and the real risk of a lost firing. Nothing staged as a 'four elements' demonstration; the household's livelihood leads.

possible_arc.opening: Dry ground, then water worked into it until it binds.
possible_arc.turn: Heat changes everything at once: colour, sound, hardness.
possible_arc.ending_open: What the kiln gives back, and what it takes. Reality decides which.

position_hint: opening candidate: a body shaped by work from the group's first moment, and a natural point for Object 7 to be acquired, if a real piece or moment allows it

requirements: An active traditional pottery household still working by hand
A complete firing cycle achievable within the filming window
A potter willing to have decisions, losses and orders filmed, not just the craft

suggestions.name: Traditional pottery-making villages of the western lowlands (e.g. around Kosgama/Meepe)
suggestions.why: This belt is known for household pottery production still worked by hand.
suggestions.verify: The specific village, household and whether hand-thrown pottery is still active there are unverified.

risks: Craft-documentary cliché with the household reduced to a pretty process
Doctrine read over the footage instead of left to sit underneath it
Economic precarity glossed over for visual beauty
drop_if: No household with a real order or stake during the filming window
No complete firing cycle is possible in the schedule

connections.note: Both hands mix earth, water, heat and air (or several flours) into something that holds its own shape.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
